chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, who raised it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let the first thing the postpartum woman eats be fresh dates (rutab), for indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, said to Maryam (peace be upon her):
Shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates.

It was said: O Messenger of Allah, if it is not the season of fresh dates? He said: 'Seven dates from the dates of Medina. If there are none, then seven dates from the dates of your cities. For indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, said:
By My Might and My Glory and My Greatness and My Exalted Status, if a postpartum woman eats fresh dates on the day she gives birth, the child will be wise; and if it is a girl, she will be wise.

key_terms.الرُّطَبَ: Fresh, ripe dates still on the palm

ai.seo_question: What should a postpartum woman eat immediately after childbirth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a prophetic medical tradition linking maternal nutrition to the child's innate wisdom (hikmah), rooted in the Quranic narrative of Maryam. It outlines a hierarchical dietary protocol—prioritizing fresh dates (rutab), then seven ripe dates from Medina, and finally local varieties—reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on both spiritual merit and practical accessibility. The divine promise underscores the belief that specific postpartum sustenance influences the intellectual and moral disposition of the newborn.
